data.one_liner: Manages a pool of Dart isolates to run CPU‑intensive tasks without blocking the main isolate.
data.what_it_does: Provides thread‑pool‑like APIs (single, fixed, cached) for creating and reusing isolates. Allows custom core/maximum sizes, keep‑alive times, task queues and rejection policies. Supports passing Flutter tokens for MethodChannel use in isolates.
use_when: You need to run heavy CPU‑bound work off the UI thread and want to limit the number of isolates.
You want automatic reuse and cleanup of isolates to reduce startup overhead.
You need to call platform plugins (e.g., SharedPreferences) from background isolates in Flutter.
avoid_when: The work is I/O‑bound and can be handled with simple async Futures.
You only need a single isolate via compute() and don’t require pooling.
You prefer a widget‑focused solution or need UI components.
strengths: Reduces isolate creation cost by reusing them.
Highly configurable pool parameters (core size, max size, keep‑alive, custom handlers).
Supports Flutter MethodChannel usage in isolates.
weaknesses: Adds complexity compared to plain compute() or async Futures.
Limited to Dart/Flutter; no built‑in task prioritization or scheduling beyond a simple queue.
Documentation is concise; advanced features may require reading source code.
data.setup_notes: Requires Flutter SDK >=3.7 for MethodChannel support; just add the package and import it.

alternatives.name: async
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides basic Future and Stream utilities but lacks isolate pooling; could be used for simple async tasks without extra overhead.
